elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement to an Affiliate without Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: Section 13.4.1 permits AbbVie to assign without Harpoon's consent to an Affiliate.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement without Vendor consent to a successor in a merger.
elements.evidence: Section 13.4.1 permits AbbVie to assign without consent to a successor in a merger.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement without Vendor consent to a successor in an acquisition.
elements.evidence: The permitted successor transactions include a sale of stock and any other transaction involving the relevant business, which encompasses an acquisition.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement without Vendor consent to a successor in a sale of substantially all assets.
elements.evidence: The clause permits assignment to a successor in a sale of assets of the business to which the Agreement relates, which encompasses a sale of substantially all such assets.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign the Agreement without Customer consent.
elements.evidence: The general prior-written-consent requirement remains applicable to Harpoon, while the former Harpoon Affiliate and successor exceptions have been removed.

elements.element: Customer consent to a Vendor assignment may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The opening language requires prior written consent and states that such consent may not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign the Agreement to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly provides that Harpoon shall not assign the Agreement to a Competitor, without creating a consent exception.

elements.element: Customer's change of control does not give Vendor a termination right.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly states that a Change in Control of AbbVie shall not give Harpoon a termination right.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement to a successor without Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: AbbVie may assign without Harpoon's consent to a successor in a merger, sale of stock, sale of assets, or other transaction involving the relevant business.

elements.element: Vendor may assign the Agreement to a successor without Customer consent.
elements.evidence: Harpoon's former successor-assignment exception was removed, so a Harpoon assignment to a successor remains subject to AbbVie's prior written consent.

elements.element: Customer must provide Vendor with written notice of a successor assignment.
elements.evidence: No provision requires AbbVie to notify Harpoon of a successor assignment or AbbVie Change in Control.

elements.element: Vendor must provide Customer with written notice of a successor assignment.
elements.evidence: Section 13.2.1 requires notice of specified Harpoon Changes in Control or Acquisitions, but it does not require notice of every successor assignment, including all merger or asset-sale assignments.

elements.element: Customer assignments other than permitted successor assignments require Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: AbbVie may assign to an Affiliate without Harpoon's consent, even where the Affiliate is not a successor.

elements.element: Vendor consent to other Customer assignments may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: For AbbVie assignments that require consent, the general provision states that Harpoon's consent may not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed.

elements.element: Vendor assignments other than permitted successor assignments require Customer consent.
elements.evidence: Harpoon has no consent-free assignment exception and therefore remains subject to AbbVie's prior written consent for such assignments.

elements.element: Customer consent to other Vendor assignments may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The general consent standard expressly prevents AbbVie from unreasonably withholding, conditioning, or delaying required consent.

result.reason: The operative redline implements every preferred requirement: AbbVie retains consent-free Affiliate and successor assignment rights, Harpoon's comparable exceptions are removed, Harpoon assignments require reasonable AbbVie consent and cannot be made to a Competitor, and AbbVie's Change in Control gives Harpoon no termination right. The fallback is not satisfied because successor assignment rights are not mutual, notice is not required from both parties for every successor assignment, and AbbVie's non-successor Affiliate assignments remain consent-free. The changes are confined to those needed for the preferred position and do not disturb unrelated operative terms.
